title: Maximum Image Overlap
description:
You are given two `n x n` binary matrices `img1` and `img2` containing only `0`s and `1`s.

We can translate `img1` by any integer shift `(dr, dc)` (moving it up, down, left, or right without rotation or wrap-around; any cells shifted outside the `n x n` bounds are discarded). The overlap of a translation is the number of cells where both the shifted `img1` and `img2` have a `1`.

Return the largest possible overlap over all integer translations.
constraints: img1[i][j] and img2[i][j] are either 0 or 1.
hints: Collect the coordinates of all 1-cells in img1 and all 1-cells in img2.
Every pair (p1, p2) of 1-cells agrees under the unique translation vector (p2.r - p1.r, p2.c - p1.c); count the most frequent vector.

examples.explanation: Translating img1 right by 1 and down by 1 aligns three 1-cells with img2.
With a 1x1 matrix of [1] and [1], zero translation gives overlap 1.
Because img1 has no 1-cells, no translation can produce any overlap.
